title: Implement output path resolution and overwrite guard
description: Create `src/lumamatch/paths.py` deriving both output paths from the target image path and refusing to clobber existing files without `--force`. Both outputs land in the target image's directory per the requirements. The guard must be all-or-nothing: if either output exists, nothing is written at all, so a rejected run leaves the directory exactly as it was.
acceptanceCriteria: image_out is `<target_stem>_matched<target_suffix>` in the target's parent directory
csv_out is `<target_stem>_histograms.csv` in the target's parent directory
The suffix case of the input is preserved for the image output (a `.PNG` input yields `_matched.PNG`)
If either output exists and `force` is False, `FileExistsError` is raised naming the existing file and mentioning `--force`
If BOTH outputs exist and force is False, the error names the image output (the first conflict) and still writes nothing
If either output exists and `force` is True, no error is raised
The target path is resolved with expanduser before deriving outputs, so `~/photo.jpg` works
Outputs are never placed outside the target's parent directory
A target path whose parent is not writable raises `PermissionError` with a clear message
Unit tests cover every branch; `ruff check` clean

steps.description: Create paths.py with the naming constants
steps.details: Define `MATCHED_SUFFIX = '_matched'` and `CSV_SUFFIX = '_histograms'` and `CSV_EXTENSION = '.csv'` as module constants so the naming scheme has one source of truth shared with the README and tests.

Coerce to `Path`, apply `.expanduser()`, then take `parent = target.parent`, `stem = target.stem`, `suffix = target.suffix`. Build `image_out = parent / f'{stem}{MATCHED_SUFFIX}{suffix}'` and `csv_out = parent / f'{stem}{CSV_SUFFIX}{CSV_EXTENSION}'`. Preserve `suffix` verbatim so case is retained.

When `force` is False, check `image_out.exists()` then `csv_out.exists()` in that order and raise `FileExistsError(f"{path} already exists (use --force to overwrite)")` on the first hit. Perform both checks before returning so no caller can start work on a half-valid pair.

Verify `parent.is_dir()`, raising `FileNotFoundError` if not. Then check write access with `os.access(parent, os.W_OK)` and raise `PermissionError(f'cannot write to {parent}')` if it fails. Catching this here rather than mid-pipeline means a permissions problem is reported before any image is decoded.

If the target path itself already ends with `MATCHED_SUFFIX + suffix`, the derived output would be `foo_matched_matched.png` — harmless but confusing. Allow it, but add a short comment noting the behavior is intentional (no special-casing) so a future reader does not treat it as a bug.

Create `tests/test_paths.py` using `tmp_path`: (a) `photo.jpg` yields `photo_matched.jpg` and `photo_histograms.csv` in the same dir; (b) `.PNG` input preserves the uppercase suffix; (c) pre-creating `photo_matched.jpg` and calling with force=False raises FileExistsError whose message contains 'photo_matched.jpg' and '--force'; (d) same but with only the CSV pre-created; (e) both pre-created with force=True raises nothing; (f) a target in a nonexistent directory raises FileNotFoundError; (g) a read-only directory (chmod 0o500) raises PermissionError.
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`. Note: restore permissions on any chmod'd tmp dir in a fixture teardown so pytest can clean up.

technicalNotes: This module must have no dependency on numpy, PIL, or any other project module — it is pure pathlib/os and should stay trivially testable.
The `_matched` suffix is what protects the user's original photo from being overwritten; the FileExistsError protects a previous run's results. Both matter and both are tested.
The read-only-directory test may behave differently when run as root (os.access returns True regardless). Skip that test with `pytest.mark.skipif(os.geteuid() == 0)` to keep the suite honest.
Do not add a `--out-image`/`--out-csv` override; the PRD chose the fixed naming scheme.
